extracted.intended_audience: researchers and principal investigators preparing applications to the NIH BRAIN Initiative
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used by NIH/NINDS Scientific Review Groups to assess scientific and technical merit of applications to the BRAIN Initiative, including mechanism-specific expectations, R21 emphases, project planning, diversity plans, cross-cutting priorities, and data-sharing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard review process and evaluation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated for scientific and technical merit by appropriate Scientific Review Groups convened by NINDS, in accordance with NIH peer review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated review criteria; all applications receive a written critique. Applications may undergo a selection process — only those deemed to have the highest scientific and technical merit (generally the top half) are discussed and assigned an overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 grant-specific evaluation emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: For R21 exploratory/developmental grants, reviewers emphasize conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge or understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 grant application need NOT have extensive background material or preliminary information; reviewers focus on conceptual novelty and potential impact rather than extensive preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project planning: timeline, benchmarks, deliverables, milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must present a clear timeline, quantitative benchmarks, deliverables, and proposed milestones for each year of requested support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines should be realistic and efficient; proposed milestones for each year will be evaluated as part of review. Quantitative benchmarks and concrete deliverables strengthen the project plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Enhancing Diverse Perspectives (PEDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: PEDP is required for BRAIN Initiative NOFOs and is assessed as part of the scientific and technical peer review evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PEDP should describe how applicants will engage diverse perspectives in research design and team composition, considering participation of underrepresented groups, career stages, and disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism-specific expectations (U01, R01, R21, U19, R34, F32/K99)
rubrics_metrics.description: BRAIN uses multiple grant mechanisms with distinct expectations: U01 (cooperative agreements with substantial NIH involvement), R01 (standard research project grants), R21 (exploratory/developmental), U19 (multi-PI cooperative research center), R34 (planning grants), F32/K99 (training mechanisms with BRAIN focus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select the mechanism that fits their project scope and be aware of mechanism-specific requirements (e.g., cooperative agreements imply NIH involvement; U19s support multi-PI centers; training grants target career development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool/technology development with broad applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for tool or technology development that has broad applicability across neuroscience research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that develop widely usable tools/technologies (rather than narrowly scoped solutions) are aligned with BRAIN cross-cutting priorities; reviewers look for potential broad impact and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data sharing through BRAIN Initiative resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on open data sharing through BRAIN Initiative resources as a cross-cutting criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should plan for sharing data via BRAIN resources and adhere to BRAIN community expectations for accessibility and reuse; demonstrate how data products will be made available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for projects integrating across scales (molecular to behavioral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the work links multiple levels of analysis and how integration across scales advances understanding of brain function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-species and translational relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on cross-species approaches and translational relevance where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe relevance across species and potential translational impact; articulate how findings or technologies can generalize beyond a single model or support translation to human neuroscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with BRAIN Initiative consortia
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are expected to coordinate with existing BRAIN Initiative consortia when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain planned coordination or complementarity with BRAIN consortia activities, resources, or standards to avoid duplication and maximize community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access and Data Sharing (PADS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for immediate public release of published research results and data, use of common BRAIN data formats, and sharing through BRAIN-recognized repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a PADS plan that specifies how and when data and results will be released, which BRAIN-recognized repositories and common formats will be used, and how the plan supports reproducibility and community reuse.
